findings.title: Audit-log GET 500s for every non-superuser
findings.body: enable_advanced is evaluated on every GET, before the optimized_pagination branch, as request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access. organization_context is an RpcUserOrganizationContext, so member is an RpcOrganizationMember or None, not the Django OrganizationMember model. That RPC object has no has_global_access attribute (global access is derived from member.role via organization roles), and member is None for some callers that still pass OrganizationAuditPermission, such as org-auth tokens. Any non-superuser therefore raises AttributeError and the previously working audit-log endpoint returns 500 even when optimized_pagination is absent and the DateTimePaginator path would have run. Superusers only avoid this because is_superuser short-circuits the or. Guard member is not None and check the role (organization_roles.get(member.role).is_global) only inside the new branch.

findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot order audit logs by datetime
findings.body: The new branch paginates AuditLogEntry with OptimizedCursorPaginator and order_by="-datetime". That class implements get_item_key with math.floor/math.ceil on the order field and value_from_cursor by returning the raw cursor number (paginator.py around lines 839-843), which is the numeric Paginator contract, not DateTimePaginator. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so any non-empty page raises TypeError while build_cursor computes next/prev keys. A later request that supplies a cursor also fails in SQL: build_queryset compares the timestamp column to that integer/float cursor value instead of converting with DateTimePaginator's millisecond multiplier and datetime.fromtimestamp. The optimized path cannot return a successful page or a usable Link cursor. It needs DateTimePaginator key handling (or should not replace DateTimePaginator).

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets crash queryset slicing
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset < 0, OptimizedCursorPaginator slices with queryset[cursor.offset:stop]. Django querysets do not support negative indexes and raise ValueError or AssertionError ("Negative indexing is not supported."). Endpoint.paginate only maps BadPaginationError to HTTP 400, so a client-supplied cursor such as value:-5:0 becomes a 500. The audit-log endpoint always passes enable_advanced_features=True on this path, and Cursor.from_string accepts any integer offset with no lower bound. The comments that the ORM handles negative slices and that this safely reaches data beyond pagination bounds because permissions are checked on the queryset are wrong: a negative slice does not succeed, and slicing would not remove the queryset WHERE clause anyway. Reject offset < 0 with BadPaginationError, as OffsetPaginator already does.

findings.title: Shared paginator silently rewrites negative forward offsets
findings.body: BasePaginator.get_result backs every Paginator and DateTimePaginator list endpoint, including the unchanged audit-log path. The new start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset changes results for a forward cursor whose offset is negative. The cursor query param is client-controlled. Previously that slice failed; now the offset is forced to 0 and a page is returned, which repeats rows at that cursor value instead of rejecting the cursor. Previous-page cursors still pass a negative offset straight into the queryset slice, so those requests 500, despite the new comment saying negative offsets are a safe optimization the queryset will handle. This is not a performance improvement for valid cursors (non-negative offsets behave exactly as before). Invalid offsets should raise BadPaginationError in both directions, and this global change should be reverted.

findings.title: No tests for the new paginator or offset behavior
findings.body: The PR adds OptimizedCursorPaginator, switches organization audit logs onto it behind optimized_pagination, and changes BasePaginator slicing, but adds no tests. Existing audit-log and paginator tests do not cover a non-superuser GET (which now touches member.has_global_access on every request), optimized_pagination=true with a datetime order key, cursor resume, or a negative cursor offset on either paginator. Those cases 500 or return a different page and need an endpoint test plus a paginator unit test before this can merge.
